How to read this page

This is a draft mock-up to support review. It is generated from the project files and rebuilt at each gate. Stated evidence (what a source says, quoted word for word with its item ID) is kept apart from assessed judgements (what the analysis concludes), which appear only from gate G6.

Evidence shown today comes from the extraction sample: 4391 items from 83 of the registered sources. Full extraction follows gates G3 and G4, so counts and examples will change.

Known evidence gaps

  • LIM-0012: English primary; Macedonian or Albanian only for core relevant sources with no suitable English version; each such source recorded in the register; machine translation flagged and capped at Medium confidence
  • LIM-0014: No National Programme for the Adoption of the Acquis (2020 or later) or its implementation reports: the Secretariat for European Affairs site had an expired TLS certificate and no copy was found elsewhere
  • LIM-0015: No official national material on the European Health Insurance Card or the electronic exchange of social security information (EESSI): the Health Insurance Fund site blocks automated access
  • LIM-0016: Documents blocked by publishers for automated download are not retrieved manually in the alpha: SIGMA 2021 and 2024, OECD Competitiveness Outlook 2024 and Labour Migration 2022, UNDP Digital Readiness Assessment, IOM migration profile, two Metamorphosis monitoring reports, the 16th SA Council press statement, State Audit Office originals (ministry copies used)
  • LIM-0017: Research and civil society coverage of Chapter 2 is thin: one think tank study (MKD-RES-2023-001), evaluation highlights only (MKD-RES-2026-001) and one human rights report (MKD-CSO-2024-001)
  • LIM-0018: Almost all national government sources are in Macedonian only (some bilingual with Albanian); evidence on the country response will mostly rely on machine translation capped at Medium confidence

Technology and AI (1681 items)

“Со Планот за намена е извршено усогласување со одредбите од Меѓународниот Правилник за радиокомуникации на Меѓународната унија за телекомуникации ITU како и со заедничката Европска табела за намена ERC\Report 25 на CEPT – Европска Конференција за Пошти и Телекомуникации. Со пренаменувањето на опсегот 2.5 - 2.69 GHz и 40.5 -43.5 GHz за мобилна служба ( MFCN), односно за обезбедување јавни електронски комуникациски услуги, се овозможува операторите да добијат на располагање дополнителни фреквенциски опсези за зад оволување на потребите на корисниците од поголеми брзини.”

Machine translation: The Allocation Plan achieves alignment with the provisions of the International Radio Regulations of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) and with the common European allocation table ERC Report 25 of CEPT, the European Conference of Postal and Telecommunications Administrations. By reallocating the 2.5-2.69 GHz and 40.5-43.5 GHz bands to the mobile service (MFCN), that is, for providing public electronic communications services, operators are enabled to have additional frequency bands available to meet users’ needs for higher speeds.

MKD-GOV-2026-003-0041 · Agency for Electronic Communications, Годишен извештај за работа на Агенцијата за електронски комуникации за 2025 година (Agency for Electronic Communications, 2026, page 51 · intervention · stated status: adopted; TECH-INFRA

Limits and alpha lessons

Active limits

IDTypeLimit
LIM-0008countryNorth Macedonia (MKD) only; comparator evidence only for the 2 to 3 issues selected for run 1b
LIM-0009thematicRun 1 covers all of Chapter 2 (Freedom of movement for workers) plus the technology and AI theme: recommendations materially relating to the areas in taxonomy/themes.csv wherever they occur; incidental references to technology are out of scope; the full analytical chain is followed for every issue originating from an in-scope Chapter 2 item or technology and AI recommendation
LIM-0010thematicMaterial outside Chapter 2 and the technology and AI theme is out of scope unless it is needed to follow the analytical chain of an issue already in scope; there is no list of deferred chapters
LIM-0011timeEvidence from 2020-01-01 to the evidence freeze date; earlier material only by logged exception where needed to understand the origin or evolution of an in-scope issue
LIM-0012languageEnglish primary; Macedonian or Albanian only for core relevant sources with no suitable English version; each such source recorded in the register; machine translation flagged and capped at Medium confidence
LIM-0013analyticalNo interactive dashboard in run 1 (no country or thematic views); a single static read-only review page (index.html) surfaces validated material and labelled work in progress; outputs remain internal analyst products
LIM-0014evidenceNo National Programme for the Adoption of the Acquis (2020 or later) or its implementation reports: the Secretariat for European Affairs site had an expired TLS certificate and no copy was found elsewhere
LIM-0015evidenceNo official national material on the European Health Insurance Card or the electronic exchange of social security information (EESSI): the Health Insurance Fund site blocks automated access
LIM-0016accessibilityDocuments blocked by publishers for automated download are not retrieved manually in the alpha: SIGMA 2021 and 2024, OECD Competitiveness Outlook 2024 and Labour Migration 2022, UNDP Digital Readiness Assessment, IOM migration profile, two Metamorphosis monitoring reports, the 16th SA Council press statement, State Audit Office originals (ministry copies used)
LIM-0017evidenceResearch and civil society coverage of Chapter 2 is thin: one think tank study (MKD-RES-2023-001), evaluation highlights only (MKD-RES-2026-001) and one human rights report (MKD-CSO-2024-001)
LIM-0018languageAlmost all national government sources are in Macedonian only (some bilingual with Albanian); evidence on the country response will mostly rely on machine translation capped at Medium confidence
LIM-0019timeLogged exception to the time window: the 2015 Law on Employment and Work of Foreigners (MKD-GOV-2015-001) may be used only where needed to understand the 2021 and 2025 amendments (MKD-GOV-2021-001, MKD-GOV-2025-001)
LIM-0021timeClaims mainly about events before 2020 are kept only as controlled exceptions where needed to explain an in-scope issue; each is flagged out_of_window with the reason and listed for the analyst. Current claims that refer back to earlier events are in scope
LIM-0022thematicDigital skills are not part of the technology and AI theme; included only where directly linked to an in-scope technology or AI recommendation
LIM-0023thematicChapter 2 is read in its EU meaning: rights and access of EU and foreign workers in North Macedonia, labour-market access, equal treatment, EURES, the European Labour Authority, social security coordination, EHIC and anti-corruption measures tied to Chapter 2; emigration, brain drain and diaspora only where directly linked; nationals' access to EU labour markets and general labour-market policy out of scope

Alpha lessons

IDLessonStatus
ALN-0001Changing the pilot country from Serbia to North Macedonia before G0 required edits to about thirty files because country, chapter, dates, languages and examples were written into the codebooks, procedures and rules.implemented
ALN-0002A scope combining one chapter with a cross-cutting theme (technology and AI) could not be expressed with chapter and cluster fields alone, so theme tags planned for a later stage had to be brought forward.accepted
ALN-0003The helper tools depend on system software (text recognition with Macedonian and Albanian language data, PDF rendering) that was not installed in the working environment and was not recorded anywhere before stage 0.implemented
ALN-0004The rule that the freeze date falls just after the annual enlargement package did not match the date set at G0: the 2026 package had not appeared by the freeze date, so the newest annual report in the run is from 2025.accepted
ALN-0005A cross-cutting theme makes the whole of each annual report and the screening reports for all clusters relevant, so the EU source base is much larger than for a single chapter.accepted
ALN-0006Major publishers (OECD and SIGMA, UNDP, Council of Europe, some Council and national pages) block automated downloads, so several core sources need manual retrieval by the analyst.accepted
ALN-0007Almost all national government sources in scope are only in Macedonian (some also in Albanian), so most evidence on the country response will rest on machine translation capped at Medium confidence.accepted
ALN-0008Acquisition relied on an unversioned working script; three recording errors were caught and corrected, which shows the step needs a tested tool.accepted
ALN-0009Searching for sources with parallel agents, one per group of families, and checking every URL before download found 99 documents in under an hour.accepted
ALN-0010In the sample, the technology theme produced about two and a half times as many items as Chapter 2 (742 against 288), many of them sector IT systems of doubtful relevance, at about 6 to 7 hours of agent time for 11 sources.accepted
ALN-0011The quote check cannot verify quotes that cross a page break because printed page numbers and running headers sit between the pages, so sound items were shortened or dropped.accepted
ALN-0012Parallel extraction agents applied the same rules in different ways where the rules were silent (repeated text, sub-area progress wording, chapter basis), which makes counts and later judgements inconsistent.accepted
ALN-0013The automatic quote check confirms that a quote appears at its location but not that it is cut to the claim; three quotes that began too early passed it unnoticed until an agent re-read them.accepted
ALN-0014Applying analyst decisions R1 to R11 by revising the sample, rather than re-extracting it, took about half an hour per source and cut the sample from 1,054 to 732 items with every quote still verified; it also surfaced the next layer of boundary questions.accepted
ALN-0015The manual extraction check was reduced to simplified hand-coding of three passages and a stratified sample of 70 items, focused on missed and misclassified items, instead of reviewing every extracted item.accepted
ALN-0016Independent agents (a blind coder and reviewers who took no part in extraction) checked all 725 sample items in under 15 minutes elapsed, recorded verdicts before fixing, and gave usable error rates without analyst time.accepted
ALN-0017The main extraction weaknesses are missed neighbouring claims (about 14% of in-scope claims, mostly low or medium importance) and quotes that hold two claims; types and references are almost always right.accepted
ALN-0018The EU accession material says almost nothing specific about artificial intelligence (two EU requirement items in six years of reports); AI evidence for the country comes mainly from a national audit, so an AI focus cannot rest on EU requirements alone.accepted
ALN-0019Drafting the taxonomy in two parallel parts (Chapter 2 and technology) produced an overlapping issue on electronic exchange of social security data, because each drafter treated the shared items as its own.accepted
ALN-0020A draft theme issue with no supporting recommendation reached the G4 package, although procedure P2 requires one, because no tool tests this rule and the drafter only hinted at it in a note.accepted
ALN-0021Text conversion left pages with a heading over an image body almost empty, because text recognition only ran on near-empty pages; one regulator's full recommendations were missing until an extraction agent noticed.open
ALN-0022The second pass added 13.6% more items on non-EU sources but only 2.7% on EU sources, so the same check may have been applied unevenly.open
